question.prompt: The product of three integers is \(60.\) What is the least possible positive sum of the three integers?

solutions.title: Enumerate signed factor triples
solutions.explanation:
Two negative factors can make the sum small. In fact,
\[
10(-1)(-6)=60,\qquad 10-1-6=3.
\]
We must show that no smaller positive sum is possible.

Since the product is positive, the integers are either all positive or consist of one positive and two negative integers. Three positive integers have sum at least \(3\).

For the other case, write the integers as \(c,-a,-b\), where \(1\le a\le b\). A positive sum requires \(c>a+b\), so both \(a\) and \(b\) are less than \(c\). If \(c\le4\), then \(a,b\le3\), giving \(abc\le36<60\). Thus \(c\) must be a divisor of \(60\) that is at least \(5\).

For each such \(c\), the following table lists all factor pairs \(ab=60/c\) with \(a\le b<c\). Ordering \(a\le b\) avoids repeating pairs.
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
c&(a,b)&c-a-b\\ \hline
5&(3,4)&-2\\
6&(2,5)&-1\\
10&(1,6),\ (2,3)&3,\ 5\\
12&(1,5)&6\\
15&(1,4),\ (2,2)&10,\ 11\\
20&(1,3)&16\\
30&(1,2)&27\\
60&(1,1)&58
\end{array}
\]
The smallest positive sum is therefore \(\boxed{3}\), choice \(\text{B}\).
